newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebel's kin abducted, judge's niece freed. [CORRECTED 23:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebel's kin abducted, judge's niece freed. [CORRECTED 23:10 GMT]

text.p: The sister of a leftist rebel leader was kidnapped on Sunday (corrects from Tuesday) in northern Colombia and a right-wing paramilitary group was suspected of the crime, police said.

The kidnapping of Nuria Carvajal, sister of Adan Carvajal, a regional commander of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), took place near the Caribbean coastal town of Santa Marta. She is the latest relative of guerrilla chieftains to be abducted.

Police blamed the so-called Peasant Self-Defence Group of Cordoba and Uraba. The paramilitary group launched a wave of kidnappings of relatives of FARC rebels in July in a tit-for-tat bid to stop the country's largest and oldest guerrilla force from snatching businessmen and cattlemen.
In the northwestern industrial city of Medellin, meanwhile, unidentified kidnappers released the 13-year-old niece of one of the country's top judges after a seven-hour ordeal.
Ana Maria Argueyes, a niece of Carlos Gaviria, chairman of Colombia's constitutional court, was taken by three armed men as she waited for a school bus.
Medellin Police Chief Gen. Alfredo Salgado said the kidnappers panicked and released the girl after anti-kidnapping police began to close in on them. No one was arrested.
The girl's father, Martin Alberto Argueyes, a businessman, was kidnapped more than two years ago and has still not been freed.
Colombia has the highest kidnap rate in the world, with one person kidnapped every 2-1/2 hours, according to security experts.
